signal: Semiconductor stocks are in a deep slide: SMH is 17 points behind SPY over a month and NVDA hit a 52-week low on a 4.7x volume day.

evidence.fact: NVDA 1m -31.5%, 52-week low within last 10 days, 4.7x its 90-day average volume on 2026-11-23, 37.6% below high

so_what: AI-chip suppliers are being repriced hard; if big customers are trimming spending, suppliers and power-hungry data-centre builders lose, and those customers' own costs fall.
ask_next: In the latest NVDA, MU, AMD 10-Q/10-K and hyperscaler (MSFT, GOOGL, AMZN, META) 10-Qs: did capex guidance, purchase commitments, inventory days or customer-concentration disclosures change versus the prior quarter? Any 8-K on 2026-11-23?

signal: Software is down again: IGV trails SPY by 8 points over a month, and NOW fell 40% in a month, matching the prior-view seat-compression theme.
so_what: Subscription-software owners are losing, buyers of AI tools may gain; the move is large enough to check whether filings show real seat or renewal weakness.
ask_next: In NOW, CRM, ADBE latest 10-Qs: remaining performance obligations (contracted future revenue) growth, net revenue retention, risk-factor language on AI agents reducing seats, and any change in billings guidance.

signal: Payments names are splitting apart: FISV +26% and GPN +18% in a month while FIS hit a 52-week low (-22%).

evidence.fact: FISV 1m +26.1%, 3m +13.7%, still 14.4% below high (ticker was FI; FI returns no data, FISV used)
Payments basket (V MA AXP PYPL FISV FIS GPN) 1m +5.5%, rel +12.4

so_what: Same industry, opposite moves: something company-specific (deal, guidance, lost client) is likelier than a sector story. Processors with bank-core exposure (FIS) differ from card networks.
ask_next: Pull 8-Ks for GPN (around 2026-11-12), FISV and FIS (around 2026-11-20): any acquisition, divestiture, guidance cut/raise, client loss or activist 13D. Compare latest 10-Q organic revenue growth and debt.

signal: Homebuilders are rallying against the market: ITB +8.8% in a month (15.7 points ahead of SPY), contradicting the prior view of depressed builders.

evidence.fact: PHM 1m +10.9%, TOL +8.8%, DHI +7.1%, LEN +2.6%; none at a 52-week high
NVR 52-week low within last 10 days, 25.7% below high

so_what: Builders are up from low levels while the index falls; it may reflect rate hopes or a rotation to defensive domestic names, not better results. NVR is the exception.
ask_next: In latest 10-Qs for DHI, LEN, PHM, TOL, NVR: orders, cancellation rate, incentives as % of price, gross margin trend, backlog. Verify against 30-year mortgage rate from Freddie Mac/Fed before trusting the rally.

signal: Big capital-markets and card banks are lagging: GS, MS and COF are each 10 to 13 points behind XLF in a month.

evidence.fact: GS 1m -12.1% (vs XLF -13.3 rel), 30.1% below high, 2.2x volume 2026-11-20

so_what: Within financials, trading and credit-card lenders are being sold while insurers (CB, PGR) and Berkshire hit 52-week highs; points to credit or deal-flow worry rather than a bank-wide rate story.
ask_next: In latest 10-Qs: COF card charge-offs and delinquencies, reserve build; GS/MS investment-banking and trading revenue trend, any 8-K on 2026-11-20. Check Berkshire 13F for BAC/COF sales.

signal: Energy leadership is cracking: XLE -10.7% and XOP -16% in a month, even though energy is still the best sector YTD (+36%).
so_what: Oil producers are selling off; falling fuel prices help airlines and rails and hurt producers. Price alone does not say whether crude fell or demand worries grew.
ask_next: Check EIA weekly petroleum data and Brent/WTI for the last 30 days (is the energy sell-off oil-led?), then E&P 10-Q hedging and capex guidance (XOM, CVX, COP, OXY, EOG).

signal: UnitedHealth fell 15.6% in a month with a 3.6x volume day on 2026-11-19, and CVS dropped 11%.

evidence.fact: UNH 1m -15.6%, 3.6x 90-day average volume on 2026-11-19, 20.2% below high

so_what: One-off event (guidance, cost trend, regulation) is likely; health insurers are the outlier in a sector that is up.
ask_next: Look for UNH 8-K around 2026-11-19 (guidance, medical cost ratio, DOJ/CMS item) and CVS/Aetna medical benefit ratio in the latest 10-Q.

signal: Railroads held up while the market fell: rail basket +6.2 points vs SPY in a month and IYT +6.4 relative.

evidence.fact: Rail basket (UNP CSX NSC CP CNI) 1m -0.6% vs SPY -6.9%, 3m -1.8% vs -6.8%

so_what: Relative strength is mostly a defensive rotation and cheaper fuel; no rail name is at a 52-week extreme, so this is a weak pointer.
ask_next: Check AAR weekly carload and intermodal data for the last 8 weeks and rail 10-Q commentary (UNP, CSX, NSC) on volumes and fuel surcharge; confirm whether UNP-NSC merger docket (STB) is moving prices.
